object: P_3 = Cay(O/𝔓^3, S_3), O = ℤ₂[ω][√3], the FS-38 §S3 representation (a,b,c,d) ↦ (a+bω) + π(c+dω)
index_order: idx = ((a·A + b)·B + c)·B + d with A = 2^⌈m/2⌉ (a, b) and B = 2^⌊m/2⌋ (c, d)
units: depth(δ) = v_𝔓(δ) = min(2·v₂(a,b), 1 + 2·v₂(c,d)) = v₂(d²) for rational d² — M53's `v2` column; M56's "depth 3" is depth 6 here; depth = m is the zero of level m

representation.scope: this tests the LATTICE description of 𝔓^m, and the norm and circle over it, GIVEN the presentation R = (ℤ/2^N)[ω,π]/(π²−2π−2). That presentation — π = 1+√3 is Eisenstein over ℤ₂[ω], so O = ℤ₂[ω][π] is the ring of integers of ℚ₂(√3,ζ₃) with 𝔓 = (π), 𝔓² = (2) and residue field 𝔽₄ — is FS-38 §S3's [hand 1] and is NOT tested here (Poros, 2026-09-13)

circle_group.reads: every generator of the orbit group is a graph automorphism fixing 0: multiplication by s ∈ S_m permutes the connection set (s·S_m = S_m as SETS, checked for every s), and so does conjugation — the three written conditions Poros asked for, first two of three

orbits.derivation: multiplication by s ∈ S_m (a unit, N(s) = 1) and conjugation are graph automorphisms fixing 0; S_m is a group (checked in full), so S·δ ∪ S·δ̄ is a whole orbit

fan_gap.ask: a proper 4-colouring with one colour absent from N[0] (FanGap; vertex 0 by vertex-transitivity, the colour by palette symmetry)

second_engine.note: the gap ask is an assumption set, not an extra edge; the second opinion below covers the forced refusals

fan_gap.derivation: at levels ≤ 5 this is not an independent claim: a gap at level m pulls up along the level maps to a gap at level 5 (`FanGap.comap`), one gap on a Cayley graph gives `Slack` by translation, `Slack` makes every pair free (D0.2 (a)), and level 5 has a forced pair — so the whole column rests on ONE solver claim, the level-5 refusal, and becomes kernel when K3's LRAT is checked (Poros, FS-38 §S3 P-A3). Above 5 it is an independent consistency check on the solver, with the planted control as its positive.

forced.legend: '.' the zero difference, 'f' free (verified colouring), 'R' refused (solver, untrusted)

separated.legend: '.' the zero difference, 'E' an EDGE — separated by properness, a theorem, no solver asked, 'c' a verified colouring identifies the pair (no virtual edge), 'S' refused (solver, untrusted) (a virtual edge beyond the edges, on the solver's word)
separated.derived_law: S_m + 𝔓⁴ = the preimage of S₄ under reduction to level 4, size 24·4^(m−4) — every element is a virtual edge GIVEN the depth-≥-4 forcing (Poros, derived and registered before the levels above 6 were measured)
separated.reads: more than the derived set would be a compulsion the depth-4 forcing does not explain (phase D's first object); fewer would contradict the forcing and is a HALT

models.note: every model was verified against every edge of the graph as built before being counted; the aggregate hash identifies THIS run's set (solver models are not reproducible across engines), the per-depth examples are the re-checkable evidence

positive_control_note: the tower has NO internal positive for the refusal path below level 5 — K₄ and K₄ □ K₄'s Latin squares are pairwise free — so the `forced` ask's refusal path is exercised on an EXTERNAL hand-checkable positive (the diamond at three colours, in `self-test`) beside the same object at four. Level 6 is where both of P-A2's outcomes are seen on one population: 15 refused and 4,080 free of 4,095 differences.
claim_scope: 'free' = a colouring verified here on every edge, so the pair is NOT forced. 'refused' = one solver's UNSAT, re-asked on a second engine and a second encoding where affordable, and still UNTRUSTED: nothing here is a theorem. 'no gap' is the same UNSAT with the same word, with the planted control showing the SAT outcome is reachable on this object. The graph is DERIVED from a norm form, so a refusal is the suspect verdict; the independent ring construction is the guard.
